newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Q1 GDP-A rises 0.9 pct, yr 2.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Q1 GDP-A rises 0.9 pct, yr 2.4 pct.

text.p: Australia's seasonally adjusted average gross domestic product (GDP-A), which averages income, expenditure and production measures of GDP, rose 0.9 percent in the March quarter, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said.
Real GDP-A in the year to March rose 2.4 percent.
December quarter GDP-A was revised to a rise of 0.4 percent from an originally reported 0.5 percent gain and September quarter GDP was revised to a 0.8 percent rise from 0.6 percent.
Most economists had forecast March quarter GDP-A to rise around 0.8 percent, for a year-on-year increase of around 2.2 percent.

The Bureau said the major contributors to growth in GDP-E were private final consumption expenditure, which added 0.6 percentage points, exports, which also added 0.6 percentage points and private gross fixed capital expenditure which added 0.9 percentage points.
A large fall in private non-farm stocks detracted 1.7 percentage points.
The bureau said the household savings ratio dipped to 4.0 percent in the March quarter from 4.2 percent in December quarter.
